Agra.x: Agra, a city around 200 km from Delhi, is home to two UNESCO World Heritage Sites: the Taj Mahal and the Agra Fort. There are also many other buildings and tombs from Agra's days of glory as the capital of the Mughal Empire, as well as the abandoned city of Fatehpur Sikri outside town, itself a World Heritage Site. Besides these three World Heritage Sites, the city has little else to recommend it.

Keoladeo Bird Sanctuary.x: The Keoladeo Bird Sanctuary, otherwise known as the Keoladeo Ghana National Park and originally called Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary, is one of the world's most renowned bird feeding and breeding grounds. The park is over 29 km² and has 364 species of birds, including some threatened migratory birds from central Asia. It is also a major tourist centre with scores of ornithologists arriving here in the hibernal season.

Kovalam.x: Kovalam, a fishing village in southern Kerala, is famous for its beaches, among the most pristine in India. This article also covers the nearby Vizhinjam, which is best known for the international seaport and the tidal power station.

Pileru.x: Pileru (also known as Piler) is a town in Annamayya district of the Rayalaseema region of Andhra Pradesh, India. Sarnath.x: Sarnath is a holy town in Uttar Pradesh, India, about 13 km north-east of Varanasi. It's famous as the site of the deer park where Gautama Buddha first taught the Dharma and also where the original Sangha was formed. Consequently, it is one of the 4 main Buddhist pilgrimage destinations, and since 2026 the Chaukandi Stupa and the Archaelogical Remains of Sarnath are listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Surat.x: Surat, a bustling commercial city in South Gujarat, is a major gemstone centre with over 92% of the world's diamonds being cut here. On the banks of the Tapi River, Surat was a major port in medieval India as well as the early British colonial times till the formation of the city of Bombay (present-day Mumbai). It is the second-largest city in Gujarat with a population of nearly seven million (2025), and an example of both the boom in Gujarat's development and a continuation of the state's historical role as a centre of the mass production of high quality textiles.
